messages:
Maya: heads up — PR #34121 is stuck in the merge window because CI has a noisy failure on one integration shard (shard8). We have ~40m before the slot closes. Can someone take a quick look? :eyes:

CI-bot: build 34121-shard8 failed — failing test: store/kv_eviction_test::evict_when_memory_pressure.
logs: ```Error: AssertionFailed: expected 0 evicted, got 3
  at kv_eviction_test:line 214
  last successful run: 2m ago on shard7```

Simon: on it — looks flaky from earlier runs. That test has history of timing sensitivity when the fixture GC overlaps. I can trigger a targeted rerun for shard8.

Alex: if the rerun is green, we still need one approver to unblock merge. Liz, can you give a quick +1 if the change looks fine to you? It's just a small cleanup in replication backoff.

Liz: skimmed the diff — looks safe. No behavioral changes. +1 from me. :+1:

Maya: thx Liz. Simon — please kick the targeted job and paste the command so others can follow.

Simon: running: `/ci rerun --job=34121-shard8 --targeted`

Simon: kicked it at 1716504442. Watch the job here: https://ci.internal.redwood/34121/shard8

CI-bot: rerun started (34121-shard8-targeted) — queued on gpu-pool-2

CI-bot: rerun completed — status: flaky-pass (1/2 flakes), tests reported: store/kv_eviction_test passed on rerun.

Maya: rerun green. We still have to update a snapshot that touched a rendered fixture — Alex did you intend to bump snapshots?

Alex: oh right, forgot the tiny snapshot tweak. I'll push snapshot update in a follow-up commit to this PR now. Won't change runtime behavior.

Jen-Ops: quick note — if merge doesn't happen within the window we should avoid a full rebase; please hold the PR until tomorrow's morning slot instead of forcing a rescue merge.

Maya: understood. With Liz's +1 and rerun green I'm going to proceed with merge in ~5m unless anyone objects.

Liz: no objections.

Alex: pushed snapshot update, CI will run again.

CI-bot: new build 34121-shard8 started after snapshot update.

CI-bot: build 34121 all shards passed — merging in 30s.

Maya: merged. Thanks all for the quick eyes and the targeted rerun :rocket:

Simon: nice — I'll file a follow-up to add a small buffer/timing tweak to that test so it flakes less.

Maya: thanks, filing the follow-up will help future windows.
